about.title: Dublin Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Dublin's mix of logistics centers, retail corridors along Dublin Boulevard, and construction tied to the city's continued growth near Tassajara Road means workplace injuries happen in warehouses, job sites, and delivery routes alike. In most cases, California law channels an injured worker's claim through workers' compensation, regardless of who was at fault. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate claim against that third party may be possible alongside your comp benefits. Sorting out which path applies, and whether both apply, takes a careful look at how the injury happened. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we're a free service that connects injured workers in Dublin with an independent attorney who can review the details and explain what makes sense given your situation, without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Dublin Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California generally treats workers' compensation as the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party, like a subcontractor or equipment maker, can still be held separately liable. An attorney can help determine whether your case involves more than just a comp claim.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter Early On
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and missing that window can complicate your claim. Getting guidance soon after an injury helps protect your position from the start.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist, But Claims Still Need Support
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim, but knowing your rights and having them respected are two different things. An independent attorney can help you understand what protections apply to your specific situation.

items.question: I work near Dougherty Road and got hurt on a delivery run. Is that workers' comp or something else?
items.answer: It could be both, depending on what caused the crash. If another driver was negligent, you may have a separate claim against them in addition to any workers' compensation benefits you're entitled to. An attorney can look at the specifics of the incident to sort out which claims apply.

items.question: What if my employer says my injury doesn't qualify because I was outside on a job site?
items.answer: Where the injury happened matters less than whether it occurred in the course of your work duties. Many Dublin job site injuries, including those on Tassajara Road construction projects, still qualify for workers' compensation. An independent attorney can review the circumstances and clarify your options.

items.question: Can I still get help if I already reported the injury but nothing happened?
items.answer: Yes. Reporting the injury is just the first step, and delays or denials from an employer or insurer don't necessarily end your options. Connecting with an attorney can help you understand what's next, whether that's pushing the claim forward or exploring a third-party angle.
